# mockingbird_mock (Resource)

A mock: an API that Mockingbird serves from a contract, with responses written by an LLM (or the faker when offline) that stay consistent within a session.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A Stripe mock from the published OpenAPI document: a new contract version
# is uploaded whenever the document's sha256 changes.
resource "mockingbird_mock" "stripe" {
  name         = "stripe"
  route_prefix = "/stripe"
  persona      = "Stripe's API in test mode, for a European marketplace."

  contract = {
    url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/openapi/master/openapi/spec3.json"
  }
}

# A mock of an internal service from a file in the repository, answering
# only for its own host name, with chaos and a webhook.
resource "mockingbird_mock" "orders" {
  name         = "orders"
  route_prefix = "/"
  hosts        = ["orders.staging.internal"]
  persona      = "The orders service of a grocery delivery app."
  llm_profile  = mockingbird_llm_profile.default.name
  consistency  = "on"

  chaos = {
    error_rate     = 0.02
    latency_jitter = { min_ms = 20, max_ms = 200 }
  }

  limits = {
    rate_limit = { requests_per_second = 20, burst = 40 }
  }

  webhooks = [{
    url    = "https://app.staging.internal/webhooks/orders"
    events = ["createOrder"]
    secret = "env:ORDERS_WEBHOOK_SECRET" # a reference, never the secret
  }]

  contract = {
    file = "${path.module}/contracts/orders.yaml"
  }
}

output "orders_url" {
  # Needs the provider's data_plane_url.
  value = mockingbird_mock.orders.url
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Mock name, `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`. Changing it replaces the mock.

### Optional

- `chaos` (Attributes) Fault injection. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--chaos))
- `consistency` (String) `on` (default): repeated reads in a session get the same answer and listed items are served by id. `off` generates every answer anew.
- `contract` (Attributes) The contract the mock serves: OpenAPI 3.x or Swagger 2.0, GraphQL SDL or introspection JSON, a `.proto` file or FileDescriptorSet, WSDL 1.1, AsyncAPI 2.x/3.0, or a zip/tar.gz archive of several files. Exactly one of `content`, `file` or `url`. The provider hashes the source at plan time and uploads a new contract version when the sha256 differs from the active version's `source_digest`, so editing the file (or the document behind the URL) is a normal plan diff. Removing `contract` leaves the uploaded versions in place. For explicit version history, use `mockingbird_contract_version` instead. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--contract))
- `data_plane_auth` (Attributes) How callers of the mock's data plane authenticate. Unset means no authentication. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data_plane_auth))
- `header_overrides` (Boolean) Whether callers may steer responses with `X-Mockingbird-*` headers. Default `true`.
- `hosts` (List of String) Host names the mock answers for (lowercase, no port). Unset answers for any host. Mocks with different hosts may share a route prefix.
- `limits` (Attributes) Per-mock limits; unset members fall back to the global limits. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--limits))
- `llm_profile` (String) LLM profile the mock generates with (see `mockingbird_llm_profile`). Unset uses the server's default; without any, responses come from the faker.
- `persona` (String) Persona the LLM answers in, e.g. `A terse payments API for a European marketplace`.
- `route_prefix` (String) Path prefix the mock is served under on the data plane. Defaults to `/<name>`. Two mocks on overlapping hosts may not share a prefix.
- `unknown_ids` (String) `generate` (default) or `404`: how a read of an id the session does not hold is answered.
- `webhooks` (Attributes List) Where the mock POSTs events after successful writes (at most 16 targets). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--webhooks))
- `workspace` (String) Workspace of the resource. Defaults to the provider's `workspace`.

### Read-Only

- `active_version` (Number) The active contract version; null until one is activated.
- `contract_sha256` (String) Hex sha256 of the contract source: the configured one in a plan, and the served version's `source_digest` after refresh. A difference means a new version is uploaded.
- `contract_version` (Number) The contract version this resource last uploaded.
- `id` (String) Identifier, `<workspace>/<name>`; also the import ID.
- `protocols` (List of String) Protocols of the active contract (`http`, `graphql`, `grpc`, `soap`, and event protocols such as `kafka` or `websocket`), sorted.
- `url` (String) The provider's `data_plane_url` plus the route prefix: the base URL an application points at. Null without `data_plane_url`.

<a id="nestedatt--chaos"></a>
### Nested Schema for `chaos`

Optional:

- `drop_stream_rate` (Number) Probability (0–1) that a streamed response is cut short.
- `error_rate` (Number) Probability (0–1) that a call answers with an injected error.
- `latency_jitter` (Attributes) Uniformly random added latency. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--chaos--latency_jitter))

<a id="nestedatt--chaos--latency_jitter"></a>
### Nested Schema for `chaos.latency_jitter`

Required:

- `max_ms` (Number) At most 30000 and at least `min_ms`.
- `min_ms` (Number)



<a id="nestedatt--contract"></a>
### Nested Schema for `contract`

Optional:

- `activate` (Boolean) Activate each uploaded version (default `true`). With `false`, a new version is uploaded but the mock keeps serving its active one (its first version is activated regardless).
- `content` (String) The contract inline, e.g. `file("openapi.yaml")` or a heredoc.
- `file` (String) Path of a contract file, read at plan time.
- `url` (String) http(s) URL of the contract, fetched at plan time (at most 20 MiB).


<a id="nestedatt--data_plane_auth"></a>
### Nested Schema for `data_plane_auth`

Required:

- `mode` (String) `none`, `api_key` (a `data-plane` API key of the workspace is required) or `passthrough_validate` (credentials must be present as the contract declares, without being verified).

Optional:

- `header` (String) Lowercase header carrying the key in `api_key` mode. Server default `x-api-key`.


<a id="nestedatt--limits"></a>
### Nested Schema for `limits`

Optional:

- `daily_token_budget` (Number) LLM tokens per UTC day across all replicas.
- `max_request_bytes` (Number) 1024–67108864.
- `max_response_bytes` (Number) 1024–16777216.
- `rate_limit` (Attributes) A token bucket. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--limits--rate_limit))

<a id="nestedatt--limits--rate_limit"></a>
### Nested Schema for `limits.rate_limit`

Required:

- `burst` (Number) 1–100000.
- `requests_per_second` (Number) Greater than 0, at most 100000.



<a id="nestedatt--webhooks"></a>
### Nested Schema for `webhooks`

Required:

- `url` (String) Absolute `http` or `https` URL events are POSTed to.

Optional:

- `delay_ms` (Number) Wait before the first attempt, 0–60000.
- `events` (List of String) Operation ids, event types (`customer.created`) or `*`. Server default `["*"]`.
- `secret` (String) Signing secret as a reference (`env:NAME`, `file:/path`, `vault:path#key`) allowed by the server's `server.api_webhook_secret_refs`; never a value.
- `signing` (String) `stripe`, `hmac-sha256` or `none`. Server default `hmac-sha256` with a secret, else `none`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A mock is imported as <workspace>/<name>, or <name> in the provider's workspace.
terraform import mockingbird_mock.orders staging/orders
```
